result:
Both solutions reduce to a choice of three subgroups, and I can't verify the underlying classification from memory, so the comparison rests on the plausibility of each set and on checking the arithmetic.

**Solution A** takes the subgroups of index 1, 2, and p in Aut(G). Its arithmetic is correct: the sum is p^{n-1}(p-1) + p^{n-1}(p-1)/2 + p^{n-2}(p-1) = p^{n-2}(p-1)(3p+2)/2. However, the criterion it cites ("p-part has index 1 or p, p'-part has index 1 or 2, not both non-full") is asserted without justification, and the n = 1 remark is sloppy. The index-p subgroup is also an unusual choice to single out.

**Solution B** takes the Sylow p-subgroup (order p^{n-1}), the p'-part (order p-1), and the full group. Its arithmetic is correct: p^{n-1} + (p-1) + p^{n-1}(p-1) = p^n + p - 1. Its subgroups are the natural building blocks of Aut(G) ≅ Z_{p^{n-1}} × Z_{p-1}, which makes the set more plausible as a classification. Note that the Sylow p-subgroup and Aut(G) induce the same orbit partition on G (the orbits are the sets of elements of fixed p-adic valuation), so including both as separate subgroups is consistent with the problem's framing. I also could not confirm that the p'-part case is almost commutative, so this remains a judgment call.

Neither solution shows a derivation of its subgroup list, so I'm choosing on plausibility and not on verified correctness. Solution B's set looks more natural and its arithmetic is clean, so I favor it, though with only moderate confidence.

WINNER: B
